newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: NEW SWISS TAKEOVER, DISCLOSURE LAWS SET FOR JAN 1.
newsitem.headline: NEW SWISS TAKEOVER, DISCLOSURE LAWS SET FOR JAN 1.

text.p: The Swiss government and the Swiss Federal Banking Commission said in separate statements on Wednesday that the second phase of Switzerland's new federal bourse statute applying to takeovers and disclosure will take effect on January 1, 1998.
The statute aims to create a single body of federal bourse law in Switzerland.

The Swiss Federal Finance Department said that the introduction of the second stage of the new law would make it easier to determine the ownership of listed companies. The changes will also provide better protection for minority shareholders in the case of takeovers.
The new law, for example, will require that the Swiss Takeover Commission be notified of any offer involving acquisition of 33-1/3 percent or more of the voting rights in a listed company.
The Takeover Commission, which will go into operation when the law goes into effect January 1, can make a recommendation to the Banking Commision regarding the offer.
If the offer is contested, the Swiss Federal Court will be the final arbiter.

The changes are part of the Swiss Federal Statute on Exchange and Securities Dealing. The first phase of the Statute was introduced on February 1, and covered provisions for exchanges and securities dealers.
